faq.q: What ways can I split a PDF?
faq.a: Five modes: Extract selected pages (tick thumbnails), Custom range like 1-3,5,8-10, Split every N pages, Split into individual one-page PDFs, and Split in half. Quick-preset buttons also cover every page separately, odd pages, even pages, extract first page, and custom range. A live forecast tells you how many output files and pages each will contain before you run it.

faq.q: Can I rotate or drop pages before splitting?
faq.a: Yes. Each page thumbnail has a rotate button (90° per click) and a delete/restore toggle. Deleted pages are excluded from all output, and any rotation you apply is baked into the result. A running summary shows how many pages are selected, deleted and rotated so you can confirm the outcome before extracting.

faq.q: How do the selection shortcuts work?
faq.a: In "Extract selected pages" mode you get Select All, Deselect All, Select Odd, Select Even and Invert buttons, plus keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+A for all, N for none, O for odd, E for even and I for invert. There's also a "Copy page range" button that turns your current selection into a compact range string like 1-3,7 to paste into other tools.

faq.q: How do I get the output when it makes multiple files?
faq.a: A single result (selected pages, a range, or one half) downloads as one PDF. When a mode produces several files — individual pages, every-N chunks, or both halves — they're bundled into a ZIP automatically. Everything runs in your browser via pdf-lib and JSZip; nothing is uploaded, and your last-used split mode is remembered locally under pdfSplitterMode.
